12000 genes is a pre-filtered or subsetted matrix rather than a full transcriptome; do not assume unfiltered whole-genome coverage

steps.question: What are the library-size, detection and clustering characteristics of the 12 lung samples in counts.csv, and how completely is batch (B1/B2) confounded with condition (control/treated) in metadata.csv?
constraints: Do NOT apply ComBat, ComBat_seq, SVA, RUV, limma removeBatchEffect, or any other batch correction anywhere in this step
Do NOT fit a model containing both batch and condition — state why it is impossible instead of attempting it

steps.description: Load /eval-head-to-head-without-confounded-batch-n6-3/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbol in first column, raw integer salmon counts) and /eval-head-to-head-without-confounded-batch-n6-3/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 3 columns: sample, condition, batch). Build and print the condition x batch contingency table, showing explicitly that B1 = 6 controls and B2 = 6 treated, and state in the output that the two factors are the same partition so a ~batch + condition model matrix is rank-deficient and no batch adjustment is possible. Filtered counts, VST matrix and aligned metadata saved as artifacts for downstream steps

steps.name: DESeq2 treated vs control (single-factor, confounded)
caveats: With n=6 per group and a perfect confound, an unusually large DE count is itself evidence of a technical batch shift rather than of a strong treatment
Independent filtering may drop low-expression genes from padj; report how many genes have NA padj and why
Gene symbols only — no Ensembl IDs available, so downstream mapping must be symbol-based
steps.context: This is the primary contrast the research question asks for. It is run because it is what was asked and because a ranked candidate list still has value, not because it is interpretable as a treatment effect. The single-factor model is the only one that is estimable.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control lung samples under the only estimable model (~condition), and how must that gene list be qualified given that the contrast also perfectly captures the B2-vs-B1 batch difference?
constraints: Design must be ~condition only — adding batch produces a rank-deficient model matrix and must not be attempted
No ComBat/ComBat_seq/SVA/RUV pre-adjustment of the counts before DESeq2
Use apeglm for shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient; report both raw and shrunken LFC rather than replacing one with the other
Do not describe any gene as treatment-responsive, treatment-induced, or drug-regulated anywhere in the output text
steps.description: Using the filtered count matrix and aligned metadata from T1S1, run DESeq2 with design ~condition, setting control as the reference level so log2 fold changes read as treated vs control. Fit with the default Wald test and the default median-of-ratios size factors; report the size factors and the dispersion-fit plot. Extract results with alpha = 0.05 and independent filtering on, then apply apeglm LFC shrinkage to the treated_vs_control coefficient for ranking. Emit a complete results table for every tested gene with columns: gene symbol, baseMean, raw log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj. Report counts of genes at padj < 0.05, padj < 0.05 with |shrunken LFC| > 1, and padj < 0.01, split by direction. Produce a volcano plot of shrunken LFC vs -log10(padj), an MA plot, a p-value histogram (to check the null behaves), and a VST heatmap of the top 40 genes by padj with samples annotated by condition AND batch. Full per-gene results table written with raw and apeglm-shrunken LFC, pvalue and padj, sorted by padj
DE gene counts reported at padj<0.05, padj<0.05 & |LFC|>1, and padj<0.01, split into up and down in treated
Volcano, MA, p-value histogram and top-40 heatmap (annotated by both condition and batch) saved
p-value histogram is inspected and its shape commented on (uniform-with-spike vs anticonservative)

steps.name: Confound sensitivity and robustness of the DE list
caveats: 462 DESeq2 refits would be slow — use limma-voom or edgeR QL for the permutation loop and say which, since permutation-null scale is method-dependent
Because batch == condition, the permutation null contains splits that mix batches and therefore has systematically lower power than the observed split; this asymmetry must be stated, not glossed
Leave-one-out with n=6 per group leaves n=5 in one arm — reduced power alone will drop borderline genes, so low retention is not proof a gene is an artefact
Some housekeeping symbols may be absent from the 12000-gene matrix
steps.context: The confound cannot be removed, so the useful contribution is bounding it. These diagnostics tell the reader how much of the DE list is fragile and whether the signal has the shape of a global technical shift or of a targeted response, without ever claiming to have separated the two causes.
steps.question: How much of the treated-vs-control signal survives scrutiny that does not assume the group label is biological — where does the observed 6-vs-6 split sit against the permutation null, how stable is the gene list to dropping samples, and does the difference look like a global library-composition shift?
constraints: No batch correction of any kind — these are diagnostics of the confound, not attempts to remove it
The permutation test must permute sample labels only; do not permute genes or counts
Report the permutation result as bounding chance-level separation only — do not present a high percentile as evidence that the effect is biological
Use the identical filtered gene set across DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom so the overlaps are comparable
Report the reference-gene panel members actually found in the matrix; do not silently substitute if a symbol is absent
steps.description: Take the filtered counts and the T1S2 results and run four independent stress tests, all on the same filtered matrix. (1) Permutation null over group labels: enumerate all C(12,6)/2 = 462 distinct balanced 6-vs-6 splits of the samples, run a fast DE test on each (limma-voom or edgeR QL glmQLFTest for tractability — state which was used), record the number of genes at BH < 0.05 for each split, and report where the observed treated/control split falls in that distribution as an empirical percentile. If a full enumeration is too slow, use a random subsample of at least 200 splits and say so. Note in the interpretation that the true label split cannot be exceptional purely by chance if a strong batch effect exists, so a high percentile does not certify biology — it only bounds the alternative that the split is unremarkable. (2) Leave-one-out stability: for each of the 12 samples, drop it, refit DESeq2 ~condition on the remaining 11, and record for each gene in the T1S2 padj<0.05 set how many of the 12 leave-one-out fits still call it at padj<0.05; report the distribution and flag genes retained in fewer than 10 of 12. (3) Global-shift diagnostics: report the proportion of tested genes that are significant and the symmetry of up vs down calls, compute per-sample median-centred expression drift, and score a set of stable reference genes (e.g. ACTB, GAPDH, TBP, PPIA, RPLP0, B2M, HPRT1, UBC, SDHA, YWHAZ if present in the matrix) for between-group difference — a coordinated shift in these is a batch-artefact signature, not a treatment response. (4) Method sensitivity: rerun the same ~condition contrast with edgeR quasi-likelihood and with limma-voom, and report the size of the three-way overlap of padj<0.05 gene sets as a Jaccard index and an UpSet or Venn figure. Output a single consolidated tier table classifying each T1S2 significant gene as high-confidence-candidate (significant in all three methods AND stable in >=10/12 leave-one-out fits) or lower-confidence, with the standing caveat that even a high-confidence tier is confounded with batch.
acceptance_criteria: Permutation null over balanced 6-vs-6 label splits (full 462 enumeration, or >=200 random splits with the count stated) with the observed split's empirical percentile reported
Leave-one-out-per-sample refit completed for all 12 samples with a per-gene retention count for the T1S2 significant set
Reference/housekeeping gene between-group differences reported, plus proportion-significant and up/down symmetry, with an explicit read on whether the pattern resembles a global library shift
edgeR QL and limma-voom reruns of the same ~condition contrast completed, with pairwise and three-way overlap sizes and Jaccard indices plus an overlap figure
A consolidated tier table is written assigning each T1S2 significant gene to a confidence tier with the stability and cross-method evidence behind it
Every interpretation restates that the confound is not resolved by any of these tests

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the confounded ranking
caveats: Enrichment on a confounded ranking inherits the confound in full — a significant hallmark set is not a treated pathway
GO-BP sets are nested, so significant hits arrive in correlated blocks and a raw count of significant sets overstates the finding
A 12000-gene background is smaller than a full transcriptome, which shifts ORA expected counts; the universe must be the filtered set, not a genome-wide default
Gene symbol matching may lose genes to outdated or aliased symbols; report the fraction of ranked genes that mapped into each collection
steps.context: Enrichment here is hypothesis generation on a confounded ranking. Its main additional value is diagnostic: the character of the enriched sets is weak evidence about whether the composite signal looks technical or biological. Human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP symbol GMTs are the appropriate references for this Homo sapiens lung dataset.
steps.question: What biological themes are enriched in the treated-vs-control ranking of human lung genes, and are those themes consistent with a targeted biological response or with a broad technical shift?
constraints: Use human (Homo sapiens, HGNC symbol) gene sets only — the mouse and rat collections in the store must not be used
Resolve gene set files from the environment's reference store at run time; do not hard-code a path that may not exist
Do not report enrichment as evidence of a treatment mechanism — all statements must carry the batch-confound qualifier
Use the T1S1 filtered gene list as the ORA universe
steps.description: Run gene set enrichment on the full T1S2 gene ranking (rank by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, or by sign(LFC) * -log10(pvalue) — state which and use one consistently) with fgsea, against human gene sets keyed on HGNC symbols: the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets) and the MSigDB human GO Biological Process collection. Both are needed as gene-set references for Homo sapiens with gene symbols as identifiers; resolve them from the environment's reference store rather than any hard-coded path, and if either collection is absent, report the gap and proceed with whichever human symbol-keyed collection is available. Restrict to sets with 15-500 members after intersecting with the 12000-gene background, use at least 10000 permutations (fgseaMultilevel), and report NES, pvalue, padj and leading-edge genes. Produce a dot plot of the top 20 sets by padj in each direction, and collapse redundant GO-BP parent/child hits before reporting a count. Separately, run an over-representation test (clusterProfiler enricher or fgsea::fora) on the T1S2 padj<0.05 up and down sets against the same collections, using the filtered gene set as the explicit universe. In the interpretation, flag whether the enriched themes are broad and non-specific (ribosome, translation, mitochondrion, general metabolic sets — patterns typical of library-prep or RNA-quality batch differences) versus coherent and pathway-specific, and state that this distinction is suggestive only. Cross-reference the leading-edge genes against the high-confidence tier from T1S3 and report what fraction of each top set's leading edge is high-confidence.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranking against human hallmark and human GO-BP symbol gene sets, with the ranking statistic named explicitly
Gene sets restricted to 15-500 genes after intersecting with the analysis background, and the number of sets tested reported for each collection
NES, pvalue, padj and leading-edge genes reported for all tested sets; top-20-per-direction dot plots saved
Redundant GO-BP parent/child hits collapsed before any headline count is given
ORA on the padj<0.05 up and down sets run with the filtered gene list as the universe, not the whole genome
An explicit assessment of whether enriched themes look broad/non-specific (batch-like) or pathway-coherent, marked as suggestive not conclusive
Leading-edge overlap with the T1S3 high-confidence tier reported per top set
If a gene set collection cannot be resolved from the reference store, the gap is reported rather than substituted silently

plan.title: Treated vs control lung DE under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample raw salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12x3 metadata table carrying condition (6 treated, 6 control) and batch (B1 = all 6 controls, B2 = all 6 treated). Batch is PERFECTLY confounded with condition: no model can separate a treatment effect from a batch effect, and no batch-correction method (ComBat, RUV, SVA, limma removeBatchEffect, or adding batch to the design) can rescue this — adding batch to the design matrix makes it rank-deficient, and applying ComBat with condition as the covariate of interest would simply remove the very signal being tested while producing deceptively clean-looking results. The plan therefore does the only defensible thing: it runs the single-factor treated-vs-control DESeq2 contrast, reports it explicitly as a treatment+batch composite effect, and surrounds it with diagnostics that bound how much of the signal could be technical rather than an assumption that it is biological.

T1S1 loads and QCs the matrix: library sizes, detection rates, VST PCA and sample correlation clustering, and an explicit statement of the design table showing the confound. Because batch and condition are identical partitions, any separation on PC1 is uninterpretable by construction — the step records the effect size of that separation without attributing it. T1S2 runs DESeq2 with ~condition only (the only estimable model), shrinks LFCs with apeglm, and emits the full ranked results table plus volcano/MA/heatmap. T1S3 is the honesty step and the reason this plan is not just a DE run: it quantifies how fragile the gene list is under a technical-artefact explanation — a permutation null over all 462 possible 6-vs-6 splits to see where the observed split sits, a leave-one-out-per-group stability count, a housekeeping/global-shift check for whether the difference looks like a whole-library composition shift (the signature of a batch effect) rather than a targeted biological response, and a sensitivity comparison against edgeR quasi-likelihood and limma-voom to separate method artefacts from the confound itself. T1S4 runs hallmark and GO-BP GSEA on the shrunk ranking against the staged human MSigDB GMTs, framed as hypothesis generation about what the composite treated-vs-B2 difference resembles, not as a mechanistic conclusion.

No step attempts batch correction, and every downstream step must carry the confound caveat into its own text. The deliverable is a ranked candidate list with a stated ceiling on what it can support, plus a concrete statement of what experimental design (samples from both conditions split across both batches, or new samples processed together) would be needed to make the contrast interpretable.

steps.description: Run gene set enrichment on the full T1S2 gene ranking (rank by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, or by sign(LFC) * -log10(pvalue) — state which and use one consistently) with fgsea, against human gene sets keyed on HGNC symbols: the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets) and the MSigDB human GO Biological Process collection. Both are needed as gene-set references for Homo sapiens with gene symbols as identifiers; resolve them from the environment's reference store rather than any hard-coded path, and if either collection is absent, report the gap and proceed with whichever human symbol-keyed collection is available. Restrict to sets with 15-500 members after intersecting with the 12000-gene background, use at least 10000 permutations (fgseaMultilevel), and report NES, pvalue, padj and leading-edge genes. Produce a dot plot of the top 20 sets by padj in each direction, and collapse redundant GO-BP parent/child hits before reporting a count. Separately, run an over-representation test (clusterProfiler enricher or fgsea::fora) on the T1S2 padj<0.05 up and down sets against the same collections, using the filtered gene set as the explicit universe. In the interpretation, flag whether the enriched themes are broad and non-specific (ribosome, translation, mitochondrion, general metabolic sets — patterns typical of library-prep or RNA-quality batch differences) versus coherent and pathway-specific, and state that this distinction is suggestive only. Cross-reference the leading-edge genes against the high-confidence tier from T1S3 and report what fraction of each top set's leading edge is high-confidence.
steps.context: Enrichment here is hypothesis generation on a confounded ranking. Its main additional value is diagnostic: the character of the enriched sets is weak evidence about whether the composite signal looks technical or biological. Human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP symbol GMTs are the appropriate references for this Homo sapiens lung dataset.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranking against human hallmark and human GO-BP symbol gene sets, with the ranking statistic named explicitly
Gene sets restricted to 15-500 genes after intersecting with the analysis background, and the number of sets tested reported for each collection
NES, pvalue, padj and leading-edge genes reported for all tested sets; top-20-per-direction dot plots saved
Redundant GO-BP parent/child hits collapsed before any headline count is given
ORA on the padj<0.05 up and down sets run with the filtered gene list as the universe, not the whole genome
An explicit assessment of whether enriched themes look broad/non-specific (batch-like) or pathway-coherent, marked as suggestive not conclusive
Leading-edge overlap with the T1S3 high-confidence tier reported per top set
If a gene set collection cannot be resolved from the reference store, the gap is reported rather than substituted silently
constraints: Use human (Homo sapiens, HGNC symbol) gene sets only — the mouse and rat collections in the store must not be used
Resolve gene set files from the environment's reference store at run time; do not hard-code a path that may not exist
Do not report enrichment as evidence of a treatment mechanism — all statements must carry the batch-confound qualifier
Use the T1S1 filtered gene list as the ORA universe
caveats: Enrichment on a confounded ranking inherits the confound in full — a significant hallmark set is not a treated pathway
GO-BP sets are nested, so significant hits arrive in correlated blocks and a raw count of significant sets overstates the finding
A 12000-gene background is smaller than a full transcriptome, which shifts ORA expected counts; the universe must be the filtered set, not a genome-wide default
Gene symbol matching may lose genes to outdated or aliased symbols; report the fraction of ranked genes that mapped into each collection
